blocks.heading: Why businesses need effective management
blocks.text: Resources and staff must work towards common objectives. Effective management clarifies priorities, allocates tasks and resources, resolves conflicts and responds to changing conditions. Without coordination, one department may make promises that another cannot meet, causing delay, wasted materials and disappointed customers. Clear objectives help staff understand the intended result; suitable organisation assigns responsibility; leadership builds understanding and effort; control detects problems early enough to correct them. A good manager investigates the cause before blaming workers or buying extra capacity. An order delay might reflect missing material, unclear instructions or an unrealistic promise rather than laziness. Effective management can improve survival and performance, but it does not guarantee success against every external shock.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Fictional Oshi Meals accepts event orders without checking its kitchen schedule. Staff duplicate preparation for one event and miss another. A shared schedule, clear responsibility and a check of kitchen capacity can prevent incompatible promises. This reduces avoidable waste and late deliveries, protecting customer confidence. Extra staff would not necessarily solve a coordination failure if nobody changes the booking process.
